headline: Court Clears Legal Barrier to Iowa Lead-Azide Detonation
deck: Trump’s stated condition also calls for Governor-elect Rob Sand’s agreement, while the Army schedules the operation for Wednesday.
body: The 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals cleared the way for the Army to detonate lead azide in Iowa after denying environmental groups’ emergency request, Forbes reported. NBC News and CNN likewise reported that the court allowed the Army and Trump administration to proceed and rejected the bid to block the Army’s permit. [E1][E4][E8]

The 8th Circuit said it was mindful of the risks from the planned detonation and said a controlled detonation with safety measures better addressed irreparable harm than an uncontrolled explosion. [E5][E6]

President Donald Trump had ordered the military to hold off until the court and Governor-elect Rob Sand approved the operation, Trump said in a Truth Social post. CNN reported that Trump overruled the Army’s earlier decision to go forward pending those approvals. [E7][E9]

The Army has scheduled a controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant for Wednesday, November 25, saying the date allows for more favorable weather and completion of mitigation measures. [E10]
The Army said health and safety were its priority. The Environmental Protection Agency says no level of lead exposure is considered safe. [E11][E12]
Forbes reported that the detonation was scheduled for Wednesday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. [E3]
Forbes reported that the court said the planned detonation’s alternative was a risk of an uncontrolled explosion without the permit’s safety measures. [E2]
